title: Cassava Root Sampling for Cyanide Analysis
author: Matema LE Imakumbili
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ydxfs7n

steps.title: Select plants and roots
steps.instruction: Randomly select four cassava plants of the same variety from the field, avoiding border plants and ensuring they are of similar age; from each plant choose three roots representing the large, medium and small size categories, giving a total of twelve roots.

substeps.instruction: Select four representative plants of the same variety, avoiding border plants and matching plant age.
From each plant, divide roots into large, medium and small size groups and pick one root from each group.

steps.title: Uproot plants and collect roots
steps.instruction: Uproot each selected plant with all its roots carefully to avoid injury, then harvest the three pre‑selected roots per plant as described.

steps.title: Label and pack root samples
steps.instruction: Choose a labeling/packaging scheme: (a) place all twelve roots from the field in one polypropylene sack labeled with the field name (later label individual roots 1‑12 during analysis); (b) place roots from each individual plant in separate sacks (four sacks) labeled with field name and plant number; or (c) label each individual root in the field with field, plant and root numbers using a reliable, non‑damaging method, then pack accordingly.

substeps.instruction: Option A – single sack: pack all roots together, label sack with field name.
Option B – per‑plant sacks: pack roots from each plant in separate sacks, label each sack with field name and plant number.
Option C – per‑root labeling: attach field, plant and root numbers to each root, then pack all roots together.

steps.title: Transport samples to laboratory
steps.instruction: Immediately after packing, keep the sacks in a cool, shaded place and transport them to the laboratory, ensuring that cyanide analysis begins within 6–12 hours of harvest to avoid rapid deterioration.

steps.title: Store samples if analysis delayed
steps.instruction: If immediate analysis is not possible, cut the middle section of each root, place it in an airtight plastic bag and either (i) freeze the bag in a deep freezer or (ii) freeze‑dry the sample, selecting the most efficient and cost‑effective method available.
